# Plan: commit-attribution

Goal: Bind every commit to the initiative that produced it, exactly and at commit time, and spend that primitive on two gaps that share it. Gap 1 (staleness): several initiatives share one worktree and one branch, so any session's push carries other initiatives' commits and their records never learn their work shipped. Gap 2 (review): closing an initiative is today an unconditional append — nothing rechecks that the execution was right, and a reviewer with no diff can only re-read the record's own prose and confirm it. The design split that makes both reliable: RECORD commit-to-initiative (append-only, can never go stale, since a commit's initiative never changes) and DERIVE pushed/merged from git at read time (git is truth for git state; the log is truth for intent).

Progress: 0/21 tasks done (0%)

## Phase 1 — Settle attribution (blocks everything else) [active] — 0/4 done

- [ ] 1.1 DECIDE the capture mechanism, the crux of the whole initiative. PostToolUse-on-Bash sees `git commit` and already holds the session pin, so attribution is exact — but it is blind to commits made in a bare terminal. A git post-commit hook catches every commit regardless of author, but sofar installing git hooks is invasive and a terminal commit has no session to attribute to. Judge on what fraction of commits each actually catches, not on elegance; the whole design rests on this being reliable. Log a Decision.
- [ ] 1.2 Resolve the record-hygiene D1 collision: git and sofar commands are exempt from the record today, and 1.1 needs `git commit` recorded. Carving it out AMENDS a prior decision — log a Decision that cites D1 explicitly, never a quiet edit to the exemption.
- [ ] 1.3 DECIDE what an unattributed commit does (bare terminal, no session, no pin). It must be VISIBLE, never guessed: attributing by file overlap or timestamp produces confident wrong claims, and a wrong "your work shipped" is worse than a silent gap. Pick the surface (doctor finding, digest line, or both).
- [ ] 1.4 Back-compat probe, the initiative-lifecycle 1.1 discipline: verify EMPIRICALLY against a published older engine what it does with a commit-attribution event it does not know. Expected: skipped with a warning, degrading safe. Confirm or refute BEFORE designing on top of it.

## Phase 2 — Record the binding [pending] — 0/4 done

- [ ] 2.1 Event type + payload, in packages/schema/src/ ONLY. Carries the sha; carries NO pushed/merged field — those are derived, never recorded (see the record/derive split in the goal). Deciding the payload is deciding what can never go stale.
- [ ] 2.2 Capture at commit time per 1.1, and verify the recorded sha is the commit THIS session just made. Concurrent sessions share this worktree, so a naive `git rev-parse HEAD` after the fact can pick up a peer's commit — prove the race is closed, do not assume it.
- [ ] 2.3 Fold: InitiativeState gains the attributed commit list. Unknown/corrupt lines skipped with a warning, never fatal (CLAUDE.md §Engineering conventions).
- [ ] 2.4 doctor: commits reachable on the branch that are attributed to NO initiative — 1.3's surface, and the reconciliation path for anything the capture mechanism missed.

## Phase 3 — Derive shipped state (gap 1: staleness) [pending] — 0/3 done

- [ ] 3.1 Derive pushed/merged at read time with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <remote ref>` — never record it, since a force-push or rebase would strand a recorded fact instantly. Decide the behaviour when the remote ref is stale, absent, or never fetched: say "unknown", never guess "unpushed".
- [ ] 3.2 Digest surface: replace the weak "N events since write-back" staleness hint with the real signal — "N of this initiative's commits reached origin/main via another session's push". This is the payoff the whole initiative is for. Must stay inside the ≤10,000-char SessionStart guarantee.
- [ ] 3.3 DECIDE whether PR state is in scope at all. It is the one piece needing `gh` and a network call, and "no sync service" is a guard-rail in CLAUDE.md. Default is OUT until a Decision says otherwise; pushed/merged already carries most of the staleness value without leaving the machine.

## Phase 4 — The review step (gap 2) [pending] — 0/5 done

- [ ] 4.1 DECIDE review granularity and who pays. Phase boundaries fit a session (3-5 tasks, warm memory, cheap fixes); close-only asks one session to audit 25 tasks at maximum surface and coldest memory. Each review costs a real session, so also fix the size threshold below which an initiative pays nothing — blanket application on a 3-task initiative is how this becomes ceremony.
- [ ] 4.2 The evidence packet, rendered from the record (a projection — templates dir only): the phase's commit range and diff from Phase 2's attribution, the tasks claimed done, the decisions IN FORCE when that work happened, the rejected approaches, and any guard violations. Without a diff the reviewer re-reads the record's own prose and confirms it — the packet IS the review.
- [ ] 4.3 The instruction half: NAME the skills (`/code-review`, `/simplify`) rather than describing bug-hunting in prose — "check for bugs and edge cases" buys a paragraph of reassurance, a named skill buys a real review. sofar ships zero analysis code and makes zero model calls (SPEC §Architectural invariants); it emits the prompt and records the verdict.
- [ ] 4.4 The verdict event: what was found, what is still open, and whether surviving findings become tasks in the plan. A review that can only ever emit "looks good" is a rubber stamp — the verdict must be able to be "no".
- [ ] 4.5 Keep review DECOUPLED from marking done. If passing the review is what lets a session go home, the reviewing agent has an incentive to pass and will find nothing. Review emits findings; close reads them; they are separate steps.

## Phase 5 — Close gate + contracts [pending] — 0/5 done

- [ ] 5.1 Mechanical tier at close, no model needed: tasks still pending/active while closing `done`, phases never resolved, tasks claiming files no file_touched event ever saw, guard violations never addressed, a next_action left dangling. This is doctor scoped to one initiative — and the exact mirror of initiative-lifecycle 4.3, which already catches "every phase resolved but the initiative never closed".
- [ ] 5.2 The override is an EVENT, never silent. A hard refusal on a solo tool grows a --force and the flag becomes the habit; "closed with 3 tasks pending, overridden" rendered in the digest forever is what keeps it honest.
- [ ] 5.3 `dropped` gets the review too — arguably needs it more, since half-built abandoned work is a bigger landmine than finished work, and today `dropped` demands only a prose reason.
- [ ] 5.4 docs/SPEC.md is authoritative: the new event types, the record-vs-derive split and why pushed is never recorded, the close-gate semantics, and §Acceptance criteria. No task is done until its criteria pass.
- [ ] 5.5 Dogfood the case that prompted this: run the review over a real closed initiative's phases, and confirm a session whose commits shipped inside a peer's push is TOLD so at SessionStart instead of being manually pinged.
